6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity
7	
8	/-!
9	# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
12	is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
13	of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
14	verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
15	index per point of `T`".
16	
17	**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
18	produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
19	chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
20	membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
21	`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
22	connection is what this file supplies.
23	
24	## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
25	
26	Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:
27	
28	* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
29	  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
30	  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
31	  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
32	* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
33	  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
34	  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
35	  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
36	* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
37	  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
38	  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
39	  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.
40	
41	## Main declarations
42	
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
44	  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
45	  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
47	  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
48	  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
50	  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
51	  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
53	  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
54	  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
55	  strengthening chosen to be provable.
56	-/
57	
58	set_option autoImplicit false
59	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
60	
61	universe u
62	
63	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
64	
65	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
66	
67	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
68	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
69	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
70	
71	noncomputable section
72	
73	/-! ## The bridge, with no chart content
74	
75	Stated for an arbitrary family of sieves on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses:
76	the coverage half of B-5 is a statement about the *site*, and mixing it with the presheaf
77	statement is what made it look gated. -/
78	
79	/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**
80	
81	If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
82	inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
83	Zariski covering sieve of `T`.
84	
85	The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
86	immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
87	then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.
88	
89	Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
90	function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
91	costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
92	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
93	    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
94	    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
95	    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
96	  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
97	    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
98	      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
99	  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
100	  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)
101	
102	/-! ## `ChartsCoverLocally` from what B-5 actually produces -/
103	
104	variable (C) in
105	/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.
106	
107	The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
108	field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
109	it, and every point `t` of `T`:
110	
111	* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
112	  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
113	  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
114	* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
115	  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
116	* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
117	  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
118	* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.
119	
120	Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
121	a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
122	four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.
123	
124	**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
125	and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
126	It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
127	written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
128	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
129	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
130	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
131	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
132	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
133	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
134	  intro T s
135	  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
136	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩
137	
138	variable (C) in
139	/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.
140	
141	The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
142	Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
143	remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
144	instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
145	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
146	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
147	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
148	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
149	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
150	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
151	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)
152	
153	/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening
154	
155	A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
156	disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
157	the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/
158	
159	variable (C) in
160	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**
161	
162	The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
163	From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
164	and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.
165	
166	**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
167	an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
168	open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
169	(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
170	the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
171	pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
172	exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
173	theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
174	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
175	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
176	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
177	    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
178	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
179	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
180	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
181	  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
182	  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
183	  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
184	  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
185	  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩
186	
187	end
188	
189	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre
7	
8	/-!
9	# THE PRODUCER: `IsChartDatumPlusFibre` for a class in the image of the sheafification unit
10	
11	## What this file closes
12	
13	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean` proves CHART-U(b) at a general test from a per-affine-piece
14	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, and its header says plainly what it does not do:
15	
16	> The hypothesis is a *per-affine-piece existence of a datum with the plus-class property*, and
17	> nothing here produces such a datum.
18	
19	**This file produces one**, and the ingredient that was missing is smaller than four successive
20	sessions on this leaf priced it: on an **affine** test the canonical field point `Over.testPoint t`
21	**is** the base-change morphism `overSpecMap A κ(t)`.  Both sides are `Spec` of the same ring map —
22	`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine` is *defined* as `Spec.preimage` of `fromSpecResidueField`,
23	so `Spec.map_preimage` closes it — but nothing in the tree said so, and every plus-class identity
24	on this lane is an identity between a class pulled along `Over.testPoint` and one pulled along
25	`relCurveMap`.  Without the comparison the two sides are not even syntactically comparable; with
26	it they are the same class.
27	
28	## The shape of the producer, and its one genuine restriction
29	
30	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D` compares `μ`'s fibre at `κ(t)`, read as a plus class, with the
31	plus-*unit* of `D`'s fibre class.  So the natural hypothesis on `μ` is that it is *already* a
32	plus unit — i.e. in the image of the sheafification unit `relPicToPicEt` — and then `D` comes
33	from `exists_cechPicClass_eq` applied to any Čech representative.
34	
35	That restriction is real and is named `IsPlusHonest` below.  It is **not** vacuous and **not**
36	automatic:
37	
38	* not automatic — a general plus class over `Spec A` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`,
39	  and `Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean` is precisely the record that it becomes honest only over
40	  `E.Carrier`, not over `A`.  So `IsPlusHonest` is a genuine hypothesis, not a restatement;
41	* not vacuous, and this is the payoff — the range of `relPicToPicEt` is a **subgroup**, and every
42	  class the chart layer twists by is in it: the θ-family (`thetaFamily_isPlusHonest`), the
43	  Σ-family, and the Abel value itself (`abelDiv_isPlusHonest`).  So `chartTwist` preserves
44	  honesty, and CHART-U(b) becomes **unconditional** on exactly the classes DAT-C's Σ-chart reads.
45	
46	  **A CORRECTION TO THIS PARAGRAPH, from a fresh-context review of the commit that first wrote
47	  it, and it is the same failure this leaf recorded one round earlier.**  When first committed the
48	  sentence above cited `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` **and that declaration did not exist** — a
49	  workspace-wide grep returned exactly one hit, the sentence itself.  That is precisely the
50	  failure mode r7 diagnosed (`docstring-declaration-lists-unchecked`) and filed a lesson about,
51	  reproduced by the very session that filed it, inside its own *non-vacuity* argument.
52	  A kernel check, a `sorry` census and an axiom probe are all silent about it.
53	
54	  It also mattered mathematically, which is why it was worth writing rather than deleting: the
55	  θ- and Σ-witnesses are the **twist factors**, which `chartTwist_isPlusHonest` discharges anyway,
56	  so they say nothing about the class being *charted*.  Since `chartValue = abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹`,
57	  honesty of a chart value reduces to honesty of `abelDiv` alone — so `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` was
58	  carrying the whole of the final clause.  It is now proved (below), so the paragraph stands as
59	  written; had it not been, the honest statement would have been "no residue beyond
60	  `IsPlusHonest lam`", with the Σ-chart clause unproved.
61	
62	## Main declarations
63	
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.testPoint_eq_overSpecMap` — **the comparison**: on an affine test the
65	  canonical field point is the base-change morphism.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt` — the producer, with the datum given.
67	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range` — **the producer proper**: for a
68	  class in the image of the unit, a datum with the plus-class property EXISTS.
69	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsPlusHonest` — the per-affine-piece form, closed under the group operations.
70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest` — **CHART-U(b) with no residue** for an
71	  honest class, and `chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest` the same open as DATA.
72	-/
73	
74	set_option autoImplicit false
75	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
76	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
77	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161). -/
78	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
79	
80	universe u
81	
82	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
83	open TopologicalSpace Opposite
84	
85	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
86	
87	open AlgebraicJacobian
88	
89	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
90	
91	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
92	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
93	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
94	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
95	
96	noncomputable section
97	
98	/-! ## The comparison: on an affine test the field point IS the base change -/
99	
100	/-- **On an affine test, the canonical field point is the base-change morphism.**
101	
102	`Over.testPoint t : overSpec k κ(t) ⟶ overSpec k A` is built from mathlib's
103	`Scheme.fromSpecResidueField`, while `overSpecMap A κ(t)` is `Spec` of `algebraMap A κ(t)`.  They
104	are equal because the `A`-algebra structure on `κ(t)` (`instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`) is
105	*defined* to be `Spec.preimage` of that very morphism, so `Spec.map_preimage` is the whole proof.
106	
107	**Why this was the gate.**  Every plus-class identity on this lane compares a class pulled along
108	`Over.testPoint` (the `chartLocus` side, indexed by points of a test) with one pulled along
109	`relCurveMap C A κ(t)` (the datum side, indexed by base change).  Absent this lemma the two are
110	not syntactically comparable and no producer can be written; with it they are the same morphism
111	and the producer below is three rewrites.  The lemma is *cheap*, which is the point: four
112	sessions on this leaf priced the missing producer as the identification of a fibre class, i.e.
113	as geometry, when what was missing was a comparison of two spellings of one morphism. -/
114	theorem testPoint_eq_overSpecMap {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
115	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
116	    Over.testPoint t
117	      = overSpecMap (k := k) A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) := by
118	  apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
119	  simp only [Over.testPoint_left, overSpecMap_left]
120	  rw [Over.algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine]
121	  exact (Spec.map_preimage _).symm
122	
123	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
124	  [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
125	/-- The whiskered form: the relative-curve comparison at the field point of an affine test is
126	`relCurveMap`.  This is the shape `IsChartDatumPlusFibre` reads on its right-hand side. -/
127	theorem relCurveMap_testPoint {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
128	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
129	    (C ◁ Over.testPoint t).left
130	      = relCurveMap C A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) := by
131	  rw [testPoint_eq_overSpecMap]
132	  rfl
133	
134	/-! ## The producer -/
135	
136	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
137	variable (C π) in
138	/-- **THE PRODUCER, with the datum supplied**: if `μ` is the unit image of a relative Picard
139	class presented by the Čech class `L₀`, then any datum whose class is `L₀` satisfies
140	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`.
141	
142	The proof is four rewrites and no geometry.  `picEtMap_relPicToPicEt` moves the restriction to
143	`κ(t)` inside the unit; `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt` collapses the affine comparison to
144	`PicEtAff.unit`; `PicEtAff.map_id` deletes the identity restriction `κ(t) → κ(t)` that
145	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`'s left-hand side carries; and `relCurveMap_testPoint` identifies
146	the two spellings of the base change.
147	
148	Note which hypotheses are absent: no witness, no `H¹`, no divisor, no degree, no separability,
149	and no certificate.  The plus-class identity was never geometry — it is the statement that the
150	two ways of restricting a *unit* to a residue field agree.
151	
152	**A measurement, not a claim, and it is independent evidence for that reading**: this theorem does
153	not use `GeometricallyReduced C.hom` either — the linter says so, hence the `omit`.  A statement
154	about a fibre class would need the curve's geometry; this one needs the curve only to have the
155	functor defined. -/
156	theorem isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
157	    (L₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k A).left.CechPic) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π)
158	    (hD : D.cechPicClass = L₀) :
159	    IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π
160	      (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k A) (relPicMk C (overSpec k A) L₀)) D := by
161	  intro t
162	  rw [picEtMap_relPicToPicEt, picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt, PicEtAff.map_id, hD,
163	    relPicMap_mk, relCurveMap_testPoint]
164	  rfl
165	
166	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
167	variable (C π) in
168	/-- **THE PRODUCER PROPER**: for a class in the image of the sheafification unit, a datum with
169	the plus-class property EXISTS.
170	
171	The datum comes from `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq` (the extraction keystone,
172	`Cohomology/GluedSheafExtraction.lean:301`) applied to any Čech representative of the class, and
173	`relPicMk_surjective` supplies the representative.  So the existential
174	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` asks for is met outright, with no choice left to the caller.
175	
176	This is the statement `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean`'s header names as not claimed, and it
177	too is `GeometricallyReduced`-free. -/
178	theorem exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
179	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A))
180	    (hμ : ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k A), relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k A) z = μ) :

/-!
# The certificate of a support-separated adaptation

The DD-R certificate lane was built around the equalizer `W(d) = ker (δ_left − δ_right)`
of the two overlap-restriction arrows.  Its two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4), and the
kernel-spanning input of `isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`, are the genuinely hard
relative content — `DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean` shows the kernel-spanning law is
*equivalent* to the flatness one is trying to prove, so no cleverer submodule evades it.

This file records the escape hatch that the *pointwise* gate opens up.  Because
`isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation` accepts **any**
adaptation over the shrunken base, we are free to choose one whose pieces are
**support-separated**: each off-diagonal overlap misses the divisor, so its overlap
colength vanishes.  For such an adaptation

* `δ_left = δ_right` on the nose (`deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated`), hence
* `W(d)` is the whole product `∏_j colength j` (`gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated'`), and
* both cokernels are *zero* modules, so (c3)/(c4) hold for free
  (`flat_coker_incl_of_separated`, `flat_coker_diff_of_separated`).

What remains of the certificate is only the (c1) data — chart-local colengths finite
projective — plus the constant-rank reading of their product.  Both are already available:
(c1) from the support tube (`SupportTubeFinite.lean`, `SupportTube.lean`) and the rank as a
sum of the per-piece ranks (`Module.rankAtStalk_pi`).

This is a genuine reduction, not a repackaging: the hypothesis it trades for is the
*geometric separation* of the chosen pieces, which the tube produces one base point at a
time, whereas the discharged hypotheses were fibrewise flatness statements over a
nonreduced base.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated'` — the equalizer
  collapses over an arbitrary base ring (the field-level lemma generalized).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated` — the Čech
  difference vanishes.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_separated` — the certificate from
  (c1) plus a rank reading, with no kernel-spanning and no flatness input.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

namespace DivisorAdaptation

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d)

omit [IsProper C.hom]

/-- On the diagonal the two overlap-restriction maps coincide: the two `≤`-witnesses
`pieces i ⊓ pieces i ≤ pieces i` are definitionally equal (proof irrelevance).  The
base-ring form of `DivisorFamilyFieldDegree`'s field-level lemma. -/
lemma toOvlLeft_self_eq_toOvlRight_self' (i : A.index) :
    A.toOvlLeft i i = A.toOvlRight i i :=
....... 140,307
the family support carries a unit equation, hence a unit overlap ideal, hence a vanishing
overlap colength.  In particular an adaptation in which **at most one piece meets the
support** is automatically separated. -/

/-- **Overlaps that miss the support are separated.** If no point of `pieces i ⊓ pieces j`
lies in the support locus, then `A.eqn i` restricts to a unit there (its germ is a unit at
every point, `RingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ`), so the overlap ideal is the unit ideal
and the overlap colength vanishes. -/
lemma subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint_supportLocus (i j : A.index)
    (hdisj : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j → z ∉ d.supportLocus) :
    Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j) := by
  have hunit : IsUnit (relResAlgHom C R
      (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i)) := by
    rw [relResAlgHom_apply]
    apply (relCurve C R).toRingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ
    intro z hz
    rw [(relCurve C R).presheaf.germ_res_apply]
    have hU : z ∈ d.unitLocus := not_not.mp (hdisj z hz)
    exact (A.isUnit_germ_eqn_iff i hz.1).mpr
      ((d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ (d.cover.mem_opens z)).mp hU)
  have htop : A.ovlIdeal i j = ⊤ :=
    Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem _ (Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)) hunit
  exact Ideal.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mpr htop

/-- **One support-meeting piece suffices.** If every piece other than `j₀` avoids the
support entirely, the adaptation is separated: any off-diagonal overlap involves a piece
missing the support, so the overlap misses it too. -/
lemma forall_subsingleton_ovlColength_of_unique_support_piece (j₀ : A.index)
    (hother : ∀ j : A.index, j ≠ j₀ →
      ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ A.pieces j → z ∉ d.supportLocus) :
    ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j) := by
  intro i j hij
  refine A.subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint_supportLocus i j fun z hz => ?_
  by_cases hi : i = j₀
  · exact hother j (by rw [← hi]; exact fun h => hij h.symm) z hz.2
  · exact hother i hi z hz.1

/-! ## The scope guard: separation forces a fibre-confined support

The converse direction bounds this route honestly.  Both pinned charts carry a partition
of unity, so a support point lying in `V₀ ⊓ V₁` lies in a piece of **each** chart — an
off-diagonal pair whose overlap then meets the support.  Hence a separated adaptation
exists only for a system whose support avoids the chart overlap, i.e. is confined to the
two vertical fibres of `pi`.  No refinement of the cover repairs this, and the pointwise
gate does not help: shrinking the base deletes fibres, it does not move a support point
out of `V₀ ⊓ V₁`.

The field lane recorded the same obstruction and routed around it
(`DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean`, deviation note): over a field every module is free, so the
certificate is discharged on the plain extraction adaptation instead.  Over a nonreduced
base that escape is unavailable, which is exactly why the flat-cokernel content of
`DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean` is unavoidable for a general degree-`g` system. -/

/-- **Separation confines the support to the chart overlap's complement.** If a support
point `z` lies in both pinned charts, the chart-0 pieces cover `V₀` and the chart-1 pieces
cover `V₁`, so `z` lies in a chart-0 piece `i` and a chart-1 piece `j`; these are distinct
(`Sum.inl ≠ Sum.inr`), and both equations have non-unit germ at `z`, so the overlap ideal
is proper and `ovlColength i j` is **not** subsingleton.

So `isCertified_of_separated` applies only to fibre-confined systems.  It is stated to
record the scope of the separated route, not to suggest the hypothesis is generic. -/
theorem supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated
    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j))
    {z : relCurve C R} (hz : z ∈ d.supportLocus)
    (hz₀ : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₀)
    (hz₁ : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₁) : False := by
  classical
  -- the two charts' partitions of unity put `z` in a piece of each chart
  obtain ⟨i₀, hi₀⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (A.toFinCoverData.cover₀ hz₀)
  obtain ⟨j₀, hj₀⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (A.toFinCoverData.cover₁ hz₁)
  set i : A.index := Sum.inl i₀ with hi
  set j : A.index := Sum.inr j₀ with hj
  have hzi : z ∈ A.pieces i := hi₀
  have hzj : z ∈ A.pieces j := hj₀
  -- the germs of both equations at `z` are non-units, since `z` is in the support
  have hnu : ∀ l : A.index, ∀ hzl : z ∈ A.pieces l,
      ¬ IsUnit (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces l) z hzl).hom (A.eqn l)) := by
    intro l hzl hu
    exact hz ((A.mem_basicOpen_eqn_iff_mem_unitLocus l hzl).mp
      (((relCurve C R).mem_basicOpen (A.eqn l) z hzl).mpr hu))
  -- but separation makes the overlap colength trivial, i.e. the overlap ideal is `⊤`
  haveI := hsep i j (by simp [hi, hj])
  have htop : A.ovlIdeal i j = ⊤ := Ideal.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mp ‹_›
  -- evaluating `1 ∈ ovlIdeal i j` at the germ of `z` contradicts non-unitness
  have hzW : z ∈ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j := ⟨hzi, hzj⟩
  have hone : (1 : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j)) ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j := by
    rw [htop]; exact Submodule.mem_top
  rw [Ideal.mem_span_pair] at hone
  obtain ⟨a, b, hab⟩ := hone
  -- push the identity into the local ring at `z`
  have hgerm := congrArg
    (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) z hzW).hom) hab
  rw [map_one, map_add, map_mul, map_mul] at hgerm
  -- both germ images lie in the maximal ideal, so their combination cannot be `1`
  have hmi : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) z hzW).hom
      (relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i))
      ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
    rw [relResAlgHom_apply, (relCurve C R).presheaf.germ_res_apply]
    exact not_not.mp (fun h => hnu i hzi (IsLocalRing.notMem_maximalIdeal.mp h))
  have hmj : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) z hzW).hom
      (relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j))
      ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
    rw [relResAlgHom_apply, (relCurve C R).presheaf.germ_res_apply]
    exact not_not.mp (fun h => hnu j hzj (IsLocalRing.notMem_maximalIdeal.mp h))
  have hmem : (1 : (relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z)
      ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
    rw [← hgerm]
    exact Ideal.add_mem _ (Ideal.mul_mem_left _ _ hmi) (Ideal.mul_mem_left _ _ hmj)
  exact (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z)).ne_top_iff_one.mp
    (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal.isMaximal _).ne_top hmem

/-- **"At most one piece meets the support" is impossible once the support meets both
pinned charts.** This refutes, at the level of the pieces, the shape the `tube-fibre` leaf
of the certificate lane was aiming at.

A support point `z` of `V₀ ⊓ V₁` lies in a chart-0 piece and a chart-1 piece, and those are
distinct — so two distinct pieces meet the support, no matter how the cover is refined. -/
theorem not_exists_unique_support_piece
    {z : relCurve C R} (hz : z ∈ d.supportLocus)
    (hz₀ : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₀)
    (hz₁ : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₁)
    (j₀ : A.index)
    (hother : ∀ j : A.index, j ≠ j₀ →
      ∀ y : relCurve C R, y ∈ A.pieces j → y ∉ d.supportLocus) : False :=
  A.supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated
    (A.forall_subsingleton_ovlColength_of_unique_support_piece j₀ hother) hz hz₀ hz₁

/-! ## The certificate -/

/-- **The certificate of a support-separated adaptation.** With the off-diagonal overlap
colengths vanishing, the equalizer is the whole product, the Čech difference is zero, and
both flat-cokernel clauses hold automatically.  What is left is exactly the (c1) data —
each chart-local colength finite projective over `R` — plus the constant-rank reading,
which for the product is the sum of the per-piece ranks.

This is the shape the pointwise gate can consume: no kernel-spanning hypothesis, and no
flatness of a Čech cokernel over a possibly nonreduced base. -/
theorem isCertified_of_separated {n : ℕ} [Module.Flat R A.ovlProd]
    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j))
    (hfin : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j))
    (hproj : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j))
    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      ∑ᶠ j : A.index, Module.rankAtStalk (R := R) (A.colength j) p = n) :
    A.IsCertified n := by
  classical
  haveI := hfin
  haveI := hproj
  haveI : ∀ j : A.index, Module.Flat R (A.colength j) := fun _ =>
    Module.Flat.of_projective
  have htop := A.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated' hsep
  have hequiv : A.Glued ≃ₗ[R] A.chartProd := A.gluedTopEquiv' htop
  haveI hprodProj : Module.Projective R A.chartProd :=
    Module.Projective.of_equiv' (P := A.chartProd)
      (DirectSum.linearEquivFunOnFintype R A.index (fun j => A.colength j))
  refine
    { finite_colength := hfin
      projective_colength := hproj

/-! ## The membership predicate (worksheet §1.2, the fibre-witness form) -/

/-- **The fibrewise h¹-vanishing predicate** (worksheet §1.2, GAP-6): a locally
certified divisor class `F₀` over the affine test `S` is *h¹-vanishing at* the prime
`p` if the fibre class of `𝒪(F₀)` at `κ(p)` admits a witness divisor with vanishing
`H¹` — exactly the `hwit` slot of `subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_witness`,
class-intrinsic by (V1a). -/
def DivFamZar.IsH1VanishingAt (F₀ : DivFamZar C S π n) (p : PrimeSpectrum S) : Prop :=
  ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k p.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
    Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass p.asIdeal.ResidueField W
        = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C S p.asIdeal.ResidueField) F₀.picClass
      ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
          ((C ⊗ overSpec k p.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
            p.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
  [Algebra k R]
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k)

/-! ## Certified families over a widened cover -/

/-- **A certified divisor family of degree `n` over a widened cover**: a local-equation
system, an affine-open cover datum, an adaptation, and the certificate.  The cover is part of
the data (it is chosen per family), exactly as the old `adaptation` field bundled its own
`FinCoverData`. -/
structure CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff (n : ℕ) : Type u where
  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/
  eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations
  /-- The affine-open cover carrying the certificate. -/
  cover : AffCoverData C R
  /-- The adaptation of the system to that cover. -/
  adaptation : AffAdaptation cover eqns
  /-- The colength certificate of degree `n`. -/
  certified : adaptation.IsCertified n

/-! ## The widened locally-certified predicate -/

variable {C R}

/-- **The widened locally-certified pin.**  Identical in shape to `IsLocallyCertified`
(`DivisorFamilyZar.lean`) — a span-`⊤` family `g : Fin m → R` with certified families over
the away localizations, divisor-equal to the pulled system — except that the local
certificates live over ARBITRARY AFFINE-OPEN covers.

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]

/-- **The obstruction in witness form.** If the support is connected and contains a point
outside `V₀` and a point outside `V₁` — i.e. the divisor genuinely meets both `pi⁻¹(∞)` and
`pi⁻¹(0)` — then `A` carries no certificate, in any degree.

No leak hypothesis: clause (c1) of `IsCertified` supplies it
(`supportLeak_eq_empty_of_finite_colength`).  So the interface does not merely make such
divisors hard to certify, it excludes them. -/
theorem not_isCertified_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses {n : ℕ}
    (hconn : _root_.IsPreconnected d.supportLocus)
    {x y : relCurve C R} (hx : x ∈ d.supportLocus) (hy : y ∈ d.supportLocus)
    (hx₀ : x ∉ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)))
    (hy₁ : y ∉ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))) :
    ¬ A.IsCertified n := by
  intro hc
  rcases A.supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified hconn hc with h₀ | h₁
  · exact hx₀ (h₀ hx)
  · exact hy₁ (h₁ hy)

21	(`Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128`), must produce a chart point
22	`x : (W : Scheme) ⟶ (V i : Scheme)` landing **in that same `V i`**, while coverage geometry
23	produces a point of the divisor scheme `D.left` with no such constraint.  The two opens the
24	route wants to identify live on different objects — `V i` on the divisor scheme, `chartLocus`
25	on the test — and no declaration in the tree relates them.
26	
27	That is an obligation *between* two antecedents, owned by no row, and it is why "close c9b,
28	then close B-6" would not have composed even with both closed.
29	
30	## What this file does about it
31	
32	It names the coupling and derives restricted coverage from unrestricted coverage together
33	with a range containment: the coverage witness, viewed in the chart source, factors
34	set-theoretically through `V i`.  Given that, the witness lifts to `V i` along the open
35	immersion `(V i).ι` by `IsOpenImmersion.lift`, and the class it names is unchanged because
36	`restrictChart` is *by definition* precomposition with `yoneda.map (V i).ι` — so the lift's
37	chart value is the unlifted one, with no transport.
38	
39	**THREE CORRECTIONS TO AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS HEADER**, all from a fresh-context audit
40	(2026-07-29, inbox `I-0894`), because each would have mispriced the row:
41	
42	1. the hypothesis is **NOT "weaker than either antecedent"**, as the draft claimed.  It is the
43	   unrestricted coverage datum **conjoined** with the containment, so it *implies* the
44	   coverage antecedent and is strictly STRONGER than it.  What is true is the much smaller
45	   claim that the containment is all that separates unrestricted from restricted coverage;
46	2. `liftPointwiseToOpens` and `pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` together are one
47	   **biconditional**, and its transport step (`restrictChart_app_apply`) is `rfl`.  So this
48	   file is a *repackaging with its difference named*, and **it closes no gate**.  It is
49	   reported as routing information, not as progress on any antecedent;
50	3. the draft argued about "`V i = chartLocus`" in two places.  **Those carriers do not meet**:
51	   `V i : (X i).Opens` is an open of the chart source (the divisor scheme), while
52	   `chartLocus C m Z lam : Set ↥T.left` is a set on a *test*.  The only bridge is
53	   `chartLocusOpens`, which lands in `T.left.Opens` and costs `haff` (= dat-b's B-4).  The
54	   mismatch is precisely what this file was written to expose, so reasoning as though the two
55	   were interchangeable — as the draft did below — defeated the purpose.
56	
57	What survives all three: the containment is genuine content (probes below), it is exactly the
58	difference between the two coverage statements (the converse), and no declaration in the tree
59	relates the two carriers.
60	
61	## Main declarations
62	
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PointwiseCoverage` — the pointwise coverage datum of B-5, named for an
64	  arbitrary chart family so the two atlases (unrestricted, restricted) can be compared.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.liftPointwiseToOpens` — **the coupling**: pointwise coverage for a family
66	  `f` plus the range containment gives pointwise coverage for the *restricted* family
67	  `fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i)`.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise` — the composite into the
69	  instance the seam consumes, for the restricted atlas.
70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` — the **converse**: restricted
71	  coverage gives unrestricted coverage *and* the containment.  So `hV` is not a hypothesis
72	  chosen for provability — it is exactly the difference between the two, and a lane cannot
73	  reach the restricted atlas while avoiding it.

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartPair
7	
8	/-!
9	# THE ATLAS IS CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS — each chart may carry its own `n`
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
12	`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
13	hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
14	"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.
15	
16	**It does not, and this file proves it.**  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
17	(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) takes a family `f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf`
18	indexed by an arbitrary `ι`, with `X : ι → Scheme` and a *per-index* certificate
19	`hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`.  Nothing ties the `X i` together, so nothing ties
20	their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
21	per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
22	per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.
23	
24	## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue
25	
26	The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
27	does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
28	covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
29	chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
30	therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
31	threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.
32	
33	What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:
34	
35	* it does not produce the representations.  `mixedParamChart` takes `rep i` as a hypothesis, one
36	  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
37	  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;
38	* it does not discharge `IsChartUniv` at any index (still CERT-Σ-gated, `Pic0ChartPair.lean`);
39	* it says nothing about local surjectivity, which is DAT-B B-6 and is what would actually consume
40	  the freedom.
41	
42	So the correct statement of the residue, refining `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s: **B-5's step 3
43	is a question about which parameters `divFunctor C π n` is representable at, not about
44	reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`
45	then the slack must go into `Z` (and its legality is open, as recorded there); if it is available
46	at every `n`, coverage can be assembled chart-by-chart against each fibre's own threshold and the
47	`b = n` forcing is harmless.  That is a sharper question than either prior reading, and it is
48	addressed to the divRep lane rather than to this one.
49	
50	## Main declarations
51	
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamChart` — a chart family with a per-index chart parameter.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart` — its `hf` clause is exactly a
54	  per-index `IsChartUniv`, so heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamRepresentableBy` — such a family is admissible input to
56	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  **This is the whole point**: the DAT-glue seam never sees a
57	  chart parameter.
58	-/

60	set_option autoImplicit false
61	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

63	universe u
64	
65	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

68	
69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}

71	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
72	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
73	
74	noncomputable section

76	variable (C π) in
77	/-- **A chart family whose chart parameter varies with the index.**
78	
79	Each index `i` carries its own degree parameter `nn i`, its own representing object `D i` of
80	`divFunctor C π (nn i)`, its own twist exponent `m i` and chart index `Z i` — the latter legal
81	*at `nn i`*, i.e. `deg_k (Z i) = (m i)·d₁ − nn i`, which is what `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`
82	requires for that index's chart value to land in `pic⁰`.
83	
84	The construction is just `restrictChart` of `abelSigmaChart` applied pointwise; the content is
85	that it *typechecks*, i.e. that the target `pic0SigmaSheaf C` is parameter-free. -/
86	def mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
87	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
88	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
89	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
90	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
91	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
92	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
93	    yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme.{u})) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
94	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)

98	family is exactly a per-index `IsChartUniv`, by definition of both.
99	
100	So a lane that can discharge CHART-U(c) *at one parameter* can discharge it index-by-index at
101	different parameters, with no additional compatibility between them — there is no coherence
102	condition across indices, because `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` imposes none. -/
103	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
104	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
105	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
106	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
108	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
109	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
110	    (huniv : ∀ i, IsChartUniv C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i)) (i : ι) :
111	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i) :=
112	  huniv i
113	
114	variable (C π) in
115	/-- **A mixed-parameter chart family is admissible input to the DAT-glue seam.**
116	
117	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` accepts it verbatim.  This is the statement that settles the
118	question `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack` and I-0660 both left implicit: the representability engine
119	never sees a chart parameter, so the forced calibration `b = n` is a *per-chart* condition and
120	carries no uniformity obligation.

122	Note what remains hypothetical here and is not weakened by this: `hf` (i.e. `IsChartUniv`, still
123	CERT-Σ-gated), local surjectivity (DAT-B B-6), and the *existence* of `rep i` at parameters other
124	than `g` — which is the question this observation hands to the divisor-representability lane. -/
125	def mixedParamRepresentableBy {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
126	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
127	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
128	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
129	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
130	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
131	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
132	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i))
133	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
134	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))] :
135	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
136	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
137	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
138	  pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) hf
139	
140	end
141	
142	end AlgebraicGeometry

theorem probe_restrictedChartFibre_bot {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)) :
    RestrictedChartFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg ⊥ := by
  intro T g
  -- the source of the restricted chart at `V = ⊥` is an initial scheme
  set VD : D.left.Opens := ⊥ with hVD
  set WT : T.Opens := ⊥ with hWT
  haveI hTbot : IsInitial ((WT : Scheme.{u})) := (probe_isInitial_bot T).some
  refine ⟨⟨WT, hTbot.to _, ?_, ?_⟩⟩
  · -- both legs are natural transformations out of `yoneda.obj ↑WT` with `↑WT` empty;
    -- an S-point of an empty scheme forces S empty, and then the two values agree
    ext S x
    haveI hWTe : IsEmpty ((WT : Scheme.{u}) : Type u) :=
      (isInitial_iff_isEmpty.mp ⟨hTbot⟩)
    haveI : IsEmpty (S.unop : Type u) :=
      ⟨fun z => hWTe.elim ((x : S.unop ⟶ (WT : Scheme.{u})).base z)⟩
    haveI hSi : IsInitial (S.unop) :=
      (isInitial_iff_isEmpty.mpr ‹IsEmpty (S.unop : Type u)›).some
    -- both sides are `g`-values (resp. chart-values) at maps out of an initial scheme
    show (restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) VD).app S
        (x ≫ hTbot.to ((VD : Scheme.{u}))) = g.app S (x ≫ WT.ι)
    rw [restrictChart]
    show (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app S
        ((x ≫ hTbot.to ((VD : Scheme.{u}))) ≫ VD.ι) = g.app S (x ≫ WT.ι)
    -- the abel chart value at ANY map out of the empty S equals the g-value there:
    -- both are values of a natural transformation whose source has an initial S-point set
    have hxv : (x ≫ hTbot.to ((VD : Scheme.{u}))) ≫ VD.ι
        = hSi.to D.left := hSi.hom_ext _ _
    have hxw : x ≫ WT.ι = hSi.to T := hSi.hom_ext _ _
    rw [hxv, hxw]
    -- remaining: chart value at the initial map = g value at the initial map.
    -- Both live in `pic0SigmaFunctor C` at an EMPTY test, which is a subsingleton.
    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
  · intro S v w hvw
    -- `v : S ⟶ ⊥`, so `S` is empty, hence initial: everything out of it is unique
    haveI hSempty : IsEmpty S := by
      constructor
      intro z
      exact TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_bot.mp (v.base z).2
    haveI hS : IsInitial S := (isInitial_iff_isEmpty.mpr hSempty).some
    exact ⟨hS.to _, hS.hom_ext _ _, hS.hom_ext _ _⟩

section Pointwise

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}

/-- **The pointwise certificate gate.** If over every prime of the base there is an away
localization carrying a certified family divisor-equal to the pulled system, the system is
locally certified.  Combines the quasi-compactness step with the span-`⊤` production rule
`isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away`. -/
theorem isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_away {n : ℕ}
    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away r) pi n,
        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) d))) :
    IsLocallyCertified C R pi n d := by
  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hgood⟩ := exists_fin_span_eq_top_of_forall_prime
    (fun r =>
      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away r) pi n,
        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) d))) h
  exact isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away g hg hgood

end Pointwise

namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
variable {a n : ℕ} {K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R pi a)}
variable {D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R pi a K}

omit [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

/-- **The pointwise certificate gate for a seed.** One base point at a time: an away
localization at each prime carrying a certified family divisor-equal to the pulled seed
system makes the seed's system locally certified, hence a `DivFamZar` class.

This is the shape the landed geometry actually produces — the support tube isolates pieces
over a neighbourhood of one base point, and every fibre analysis reads at a single prime —
so no globally valid no-leak hypothesis (false in general, I-0209) is required anywhere. -/
theorem isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_away_certified (hD : D.IsGenerator)
    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away r) pi n,
        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
          ((D.localEquations hD).pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) (D.localEquations hD)))) :
    IsLocallyCertified C R pi n (D.localEquations hD) :=
  isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_away h

/-- **The gate in its most consumable form: certify the pulled system after shrinking.**
At every prime it suffices to produce an `r ∉ p` and a certificate for *some* adaptation
of the pulled seed system over `Localization.Away r`.  The adaptation itself is free
(`exists_divisorAdaptation`), so the only genuine obligation is the certificate over the
shrunken base — where the support tube makes per-piece isolation available.

Contrast with the old gate `divisorAdaptation_isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`,
which demanded a certificate for the *canonically extracted* adaptation over the whole
chart ring; that shape forces a globally valid no-leak hypothesis, which is false. -/
theorem isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation
    (hD : D.IsGenerator)
    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
      ∃ A : DivisorAdaptation C (Localization.Away r) pi
          ((D.localEquations hD).pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) (D.localEquations hD))),
        A.IsCertified n) :
    IsLocallyCertified C R pi n (D.localEquations hD) := by
  refine isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_away_certified hD fun p => ?_
  obtain ⟨r, hrp, A, hA⟩ := h p
  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
  -- bundle the supplied adaptation and its certificate; the divisor equality is `rfl`
  exact ⟨r, hrp, ⟨_, A, hA⟩, Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl _⟩

/-- The `DivFamZar` class of a seed certified pointwise on the base. -/
noncomputable def divFamZar_of_forall_prime_away_certified (hD : D.IsGenerator)
    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away r) pi n,
        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
          ((D.localEquations hD).pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) (D.localEquations hD)))) :
    DivFamZar C R pi n :=
  DivFamZar.mk (D.localEquations hD)
    (isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_away_certified hD h)

end ThetaGeneratorSeed

=== LocusIsOpen 160-200
`BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `A` whose fibre witness predicate at every residue field agrees
with the split witness predicate of `μ` at the corresponding point.

Two remarks on the shape, both deliberate:

* it is stated as an **agreement of predicates at every point**, not as a class equality.
  That is weaker than "the datum's class is `μ`", and it is all the openness argument
  consumes — which matters, because the class equality is what needs `cechPicClass_inv` and
  a class-level identification, whereas a lane that can produce the pointwise agreement by any
  other route may use this theorem immediately;
* the split predicate is read at `Over.testPoint`, i.e. at the canonical residue-field point
  of the affine test, so no choice of affine chart enters;
* the `Algebra A (testPointField t)` / `IsScalarTower k A (testPointField t)` instances the
  datum predicate needs are the **canonical** ones of `Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean`.  An
  earlier draft of this file carried them as explicit `alg`/`tow` arguments; that was strictly
  worse — it made the statement false for some regradings (`HasWitnessH1Vanishing` reads its
  `Algebra` instance inside `relCurveMap`, so a non-canonical `alg` names a different set) as
  well as unusable. -/
def IsChartDatumPresentation {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : (overSpec k A).left,
    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
      ↔ IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)

/-! ## The carrier translation: `testPointField` on `Spec A` versus `Ideal.ResidueField`

The engine's open set lives in `PrimeSpectrum A` and is indexed by `q.asIdeal.ResidueField`;
`chartLocus` lives in `(overSpec k A).left = Spec A` and is indexed by `Over.testPointField`.
The two carriers are the same space, but the two *fields* are only canonically isomorphic
(mathlib's `Spec.residueFieldIso`), so the witness predicate has to be carried across that
isomorphism.  That is what this section does, and it is the transport the (b-amendment) folds
into "affine pieces glue by (V1c)-style locality". -/

`Over.testPointField t` is the *scheme* residue field `(Spec A).residueField t`, while every
engine-facing predicate reads the *algebraic* residue field `t.asIdeal.ResidueField` of the

the form the tower needs, namely that the canonical `A`-algebra structure on the scheme
residue field (`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`) factors through the algebraic one.
